authors: Hosseini, S. A.; Smadi, O.
title: How prediction accuracy can affect the decision-making process in pavement management system
note: THE bridge citation. Injects 10-90% prediction error and prices the consequence in treatment cost over 20 years. This is the paper that lets §11 say why the rigour audit matters in money rather than in R2 — build the argument of §11 around it.

authors: Pasupunuri, S. K.; Thom, N.; Li, L.
title: Roughness prediction of jointed plain concrete pavement using physics informed neural networks
note: Uses the MEPDG roughness model itself as the physics loss term. The clearest published case of mechanics-constrained learning in pavement; MAE 0.134, R2 0.90. Central to the §10 argument that constraint beats post-hoc explanation.

authors: Zeiada, W.; Obaid, L.; El-Badawy, S. M.; et al.
title: Benchmarking classical and deep machine learning models for predicting hot mix asphalt dynamic modulus
data_source: laboratory (50 AC mixtures, Saudi Arabia + Idaho)
note: EXEMPLARY. Benchmarks against Witczak NCHRP 1-37A, 1-40D and Hirsch — real mechanistic baselines, not straw men. Also scores models on complexity and physical rationality, not accuracy alone. Bagging ensembles win, not the deep nets. Use as the positive template in §11 and §12.

authors: Alnaqbi, A.; Zeiada, W.; Al-Khateeb, G. G.
title: A hybrid machine learning method of support vector regression with particle swarm optimization for predicting IRI in continuously reinforced concrete pavement
note: Same 33-CRCP-section LTPP substrate as Alnaqbi 2026 GBM-PSO paper already in the database — a second report from an overlapping data source. R2=0.991 under 5-fold CV; unless section-blocked, a leakage-risk case identical in structure to the earlier one. Flag both for the §8/§11 near-duplicate-substrate discussion.

authors: Ghorbani, B.; Arulrajah, A.; Narsilio, G. A.; et al.
title: Development of genetic-based models for predicting the resilient modulus of cohesive pavement subgrade soils
architecture: ANN-GA (GA on weights) vs. GA symbolic
note: Directly compares a symbolic GA-only model against an ANN-GA hybrid on the SAME data — one of the few true head-to-head H2-vs-H7 comparisons in the corpus. Central to the premium analysis.

authors: Huang, H.; Xu, Z.; Li, X.; et al.
title: Predicting rheological properties of asphalt modified with mineral powder: bagging, boosting, and stacking vs. single machine learning models
note: States explicitly that the stacking framework uses CROSS-VALIDATED base-model predictions as meta-learner input specifically to reduce information leakage. This is the clearest positive H5 exemplar in the corpus and becomes the worked 'good practice' case in PAVE-ML item 12a-with-stacking (§10).

authors: Mazari, M.; Rodriguez, D. D.
title: Prediction of pavement roughness using a hybrid gene expression programming-neural network technique
note: Early (2016), heavily cited (159) H7 case: symbolic GEP feeds a neural refinement stage. Good anchor for the symbolic-numeric taxonomy entry.

authors: Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Heidarabadizadeh, N.; Jalali, F.; Tavana Amlashi, A.; Papagiannakis, A. T.
title: METABACKCAL: Implementing metaheuristic-driven back-calculation for flexible pavement moduli estimation
note: Direct 2025 successor to the 2020 ANN back-calculation paper. A named, released tool is deployment evidence — one of the few in the corpus. Anchor of §5.

authors: Yao, L.; Leng, Z.; Jiang, J.; et al.
title: Large-scale maintenance and rehabilitation optimization for multi-lane highway asphalt pavement: A reinforcement learning approach
data_source: real-world highway network + probabilistic deterioration models
deployment_evidence: applied to a real network (26.6% cost saving vs practice)
note: Integrates LCA and LCCA into the reward and propagates deterioration uncertainty. One of the strongest deployment-facing studies in the corpus.

authors: Al Zubi, M.; Ahmad, M.; Abdullah, S.; et al.
title: Long short term memory networks for predicting resilient modulus of stabilized base material subject to wet-dry cycles
note: Architecture-task mismatch candidate: LSTM applied to non-sequential tabular records, R2=0.995/0.980. Examine for leakage and baseline strength in full text.

authors: Guo, M.; Zhou, M.; Du, X.; et al.
title: Machine learning-based analysis of interaction effects among influencing factors on the resilient modulus of stabilized aggregate base
note: Best-practice case for interaction analysis; ensemble trees beating ANNs on tabular data — a §4 theme.

authors: Louzi, N.; Al-Jamal, M. Q.; AlJamal, M.
title: A novel simulation-oriented thermo-hydro-mechanical artificial intelligence framework for reliability assessment of energy-embedded pavement structures
note: Pavement layers as graph nodes — the most explicit structural inductive bias found so far. R2=0.994 on synthetic data only; the §11 question is whether it transfers to field data at all.

authors: Cha, Y.-J.; Choi, W.; Büyüköztürk, O.
title: Deep learning-based crack damage detection using convolutional neural networks
note: The citation anchor of the whole vision stream; ~392 citations in 2025 alone.

authors: Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Tavana Amlashi, A.; Bahrami, A.; et al.
title: A formulation for asphalt concrete air void during service life by adopting a hybrid evolutionary polynomial regression and multi-gene genetic programming
note: Symbolic-regression counterpoint to opaque learners; supports the §10 argument.

authors: Safi Jahanshahi, F.; Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Naseri, H.; Mouldi, A.
title: Interpretable AI models based on hybrid ensemble learning methods for predicting unconfined compressive strength of cement-stabilized magnetite iron ore tailing
note: Deployment evidence (GUI) — one of the few. Directly supports §12/PAVE-ML deployment item.

authors: Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Heidarabadizadeh, N.; Jalali, F.
title: Artificial neural network back-calculation of flexible pavements with sensitivity analysis using Garson's and connection weights algorithms
note: Anchor for the inverse-problem section and for pre-SHAP interpretability lineage.

authors: Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Fakhri, M.
title: Quasi-static analysis of flexible pavements based on predicted frequencies using Fast Fourier Transform and Artificial Neural Network
data_source: simulated (1200 sections) + Virginia Smart Road field check
note: Rare and valuable: synthetic training WITH an independent field comparison. Positive exemplar for §11.

authors: Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Fakhri, M.
title: Prediction of frequency for simulation of asphalt mix fatigue tests using MARS and ANN
note: Early example of pairing a black-box with an intrinsically interpretable model — theme of §10.

authors: Cavalli, M. C.; Chen, D.; Chen, Q.; et al. (39 authors)
title: Review of advanced road materials, structures, equipment, and detection technologies
note: Omnibus; AI is one strand among many — leaves our niche open.

authors: Rasol, M.; Pais, J. C.; Pérez-Gracia, V.; et al.
title: GPR monitoring for road transport infrastructure: A systematic review and machine learning insights

authors: Cao, W.; Liu, Q.; He, Z.
title: Review of pavement defect detection methods
note: Benchmark-and-metric comparison; useful source for our §7 comparability critique.

authors: Hou, Y.; Li, Q.; Zhang, C.; et al.
title: The state-of-the-art review on applications of intrusive sensing, image processing techniques, and machine learning methods in pavement monitoring and analysis

authors: Gopalakrishnan, K.
title: Deep learning in data-driven pavement image analysis and automated distress detection: A review
note: Narrative review; owns the early DL-vision territory.

authors: M'harzi Alaoui, F. e.; Taki, Y.; Aalil, I.; et al.
title: From lab to algorithm: a review of AI-driven predictive modeling in soil stabilization for road construction
venue: J. Umm Al-Qura Univ. Eng. Archit.
note: CRITICAL. Names the 'lab-to-field performance gap' and the 'interpretability paradox of opaque high-accuracy models'. Same diagnosis as our §11, but restricted to soil stabilisation and without a coding rubric or instrument. Our differentiation: whole-of-pavement scope + quantified per-study rigour audit + PAVE-ML. Cite prominently and honestly.

authors: Yang, X.; Guan, J.; Ding, L.; et al.
title: Research and applications of artificial neural network in pavement engineering: A state-of-the-art review
note: Defines the gap we must clear. Stops at MLP/CNN/RNN; no rigour audit; pre-dates the hybrid/XAI/transformer wave.

authors: Abambres, M.; Ferreira, A.
title: Application of ANN in pavement engineering: State-of-art
note: Preprint only, 2 citations. Further evidence that the generic title space is saturated — supports the repositioning decision.

authors: Tamagusko, T.; Ferreira, A.
title: Machine learning for prediction of the international roughness index on flexible pavements: A review, challenges, and future directions
note: IMPORTANT: reports input-variable prevalence (traffic 89%, structure/climate 78%, M&R history 33%) and names standardisation, interpretability and replicability as open. Occupies part of our critique territory for IRI/flexible. Must be cited and differentiated explicitly in §1.

authors: Zagvozda, M.; Ljutić, K.; Janić, V.; et al.
title: AI for pavement distress detection on lower-ranking roads: A bibliometric and systematic review
note: Confirms the ground-truthing and benchmark-standardisation gaps we intend to quantify.

authors: Hariri Asli, H.; Brake, N.; Nikookar, M.; et al.
title: Application of artificial intelligence methods in the international roughness index prediction of rigid and composite pavements: a systematic review
note: Narrow slice of our §8; cite as evidence of LTPP dependency, do not overlap scope.

authors: Deng, Y.; Shi, X.
title: Modeling the rutting performance of asphalt pavements: a review
note: Includes a practitioner survey of which rutting models agencies actually use — a rare deployment-side data point, cite in §11/§9.

authors: Yuan, Q.; Shi, Y.; Li, M.
title: A review of computer vision-based crack detection methods in civil infrastructure: Progress and challenges

authors: Safyari, Y.; Mahdianpari, M.; Shiri, H.
title: A review of vision-based pothole detection methods using computer vision and machine learning

authors: Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Salehi, M.; Mamou, A.; et al.
title: Investigation of subgrade stabilization life-extending benefits in flexible pavements using a non-linear mechanistic-empirical analysis
note: Not an ML paper, but valuable: gives the mechanistic reference behaviour that data-driven subgrade models should reproduce. Use in §11 to argue that mechanistic consistency is a testable criterion, not a slogan.

authors: Ghanizadeh, A. R.; Aziminejad, A.; Asteris, P. G.; et al.
title: Soft computing to predict earthquake-induced soil liquefaction via CPT results
note: n=109 with 99.09% accuracy — exactly the small-n/high-skill pattern §11 examines; use as a candid methodological discussion point, not as a target.

authors: Baduge, S. K.; Thilakarathna, S.; Perera, J. S.; et al.
title: Artificial intelligence and smart vision for building and construction 4.0: Machine and deep learning methods and applications
note: Shows the style and depth Automation in Construction rewards in a review.

authors: Alzubaidi, L.; Bai, J.; Al-Sabaawi, A.; et al.
title: A survey on deep learning tools dealing with data scarcity: definitions, challenges, solutions, tips, and applications
note: Source for the data-scarcity remedies we recommend importing into pavement work.

authors: Hua, W.; Yu, Q.; Xiao, Y.; et al.
title: Development of artificial-neural-network-based permanent deformation prediction model of unbound granular materials subjected to moving wheel loading

authors: Khan, K.; Jalal, F. E.; Khan, M. A.; et al.
title: Prediction models for evaluating resilient modulus of stabilized aggregate bases in wet and dry alternating environments: ANN and GEP approaches
note: Same dataset family as Al Zubi 2024 and Guo 2025 — a near-duplicate-substrate cluster worth naming explicitly in §8/§11.

authors: Vargas, C. A.; El Hanandeh, A.
title: Features importance and their impacts on the properties of asphalt mixture modified with plastic waste: A machine learning modeling approach
note: Rare example of a paper that converts feature importance into a reporting recommendation for future experimental work — a model for what §12 asks the field to do.

authors: Duan, X.
title: Assessment of resilient modulus of soil using hybrid extreme gradient boosting models
note: R2=0.995 against nine comparators — check baseline tuning parity in full text.

authors: Kaloop, M. R.; Kumar, D.; Samui, P.; et al.
title: Particle swarm optimization algorithm-extreme learning machine (PSO-ELM) model for predicting resilient modulus of stabilized aggregate bases

authors: Azam, A.; Bardhan, A.; Kaloop, M. R.; et al.
title: Modeling resilient modulus of subgrade soils using LSSVM optimized with swarm intelligence algorithms
note: Six-metaheuristic bake-off; the differences between winners are within noise — a §11 talking point about over-claimed hybrid gains.

authors: Cheng, C.; Wang, L.; Zhou, X.; et al.
title: Predicting rutting development using machine learning methods based on RIOHTrack data
architecture: SVR / ANN / GBDT / RF / Extra Trees
note: Full-scale APT data rather than LTPP — a rare escape from the shared-substrate problem. Compares against the M-E rutting model.

authors: Baldo, N.; Miani, M.; Rondinella, F.; et al.
title: A machine learning approach to determine airport asphalt concrete layer moduli using heavy weight deflectometer data
note: Data augmentation on a small field set — leakage risk to assess carefully in full text.

authors: Elbagalati, O.; Mousa, M. R.; Elseifi, M. A.; et al.
title: Development of a methodology to backcalculate pavement layer moduli using the traffic speed deflectometer

authors: Leiva-Villacorta, F.; Vargas-Nordcbeck, A.; Timm, D. H.
title: Non-destructive evaluation of sustainable pavement technologies using artificial neural networks
note: Forward-calculation under bonded vs. slip interface — a genuinely mechanistic use of ANN.

authors: Elbagalati, O.; Elseifi, M. A.; Gaspard, K.; et al.
title: Development of an artificial neural network model to predict subgrade resilient modulus from continuous deflection testing
note: EXTERNAL VALIDATION: trained on Louisiana, validated on an independent Minnesota programme (R2 0.73 -> 0.72). This is the standard §11 argues the field should meet.

authors: Ali, L.; Al Jassmi, H.; Swavaf, M.; et al.
title: Rs-Net: Residual Sharp U-Net architecture for pavement crack segmentation and severity assessment
note: Reports accuracy >0.97 on a class-imbalanced segmentation task — pixel accuracy is near-meaningless when cracks occupy a few percent of pixels. Direct evidence for the §7 metric-misuse argument.

authors: Sun, Z.; Zhai, J.; Pei, L.; et al.
title: Automatic pavement crack detection transformer based on convolutional and sequential feature fusion
note: AP 45.6% on the authors' own set vs 45.8% on COCO — the near-identical figures across radically different domains deserve scrutiny.

authors: Katsamenis, I.; Sakelliou, A.; Bakalos, N.; et al.
title: Deep transformer networks for precise pothole segmentation tasks
note: SegFormer vs U-Net, F1 ~80%. Reports F1 rather than pixel accuracy — better practice than most of the segmentation literature.

authors: Wang, N.; Shang, L.; Song, X.
title: A transformer-optimized deep learning network for road damage detection and tracking

authors: Liu, G.; Ding, W.; Shu, J.; et al.
title: Two-stream boundary-aware neural network for concrete crack segmentation and quantification
architecture: HRNet + dynamic feature fusion edge branch
note: mIoU reported separately for pure-crack (79.3%), complex-background (68.7%) and variable-width (70.3%) scenarios. Stratified reporting like this is what makes cross-study comparison possible — another PAVE-ML item.

authors: Dorafshan, S.; Thomas, R. J.; Maguire, M.
title: Comparison of deep convolutional neural networks and edge detectors for image-based crack detection in concrete
note: One of the few papers that benchmarks DL against a genuinely tuned classical baseline. Model case for the §11 baseline-strength criterion.

authors: Zhang, Z.; Song, W.; Zhuang, Y.; et al.
title: Automated multi-type pavement distress segmentation and quantification using transformer networks for pavement condition index prediction
architecture: mix transformer (MiT) encoder + mixed attention decoder
note: One of the few studies that carries segmentation output through to an engineering index (PCI) rather than stopping at IoU. Bridges §7 and §8 — exactly the linkage §11 finds missing.

authors: Li, Z.; Zhang, T.; Miao, Y.; et al.
title: Automated quantification of crack length and width in asphalt pavements
note: Moves from segmentation mask to engineering quantity (length 80.2%, width 84.3% accuracy) and reports runtime. Reporting runtime at all is unusual and should be a PAVE-ML item.

authors: Zhou, J.; Zhou, M.; Wang, Q.; et al.
title: Predicting the international roughness index of JPCP and CRCP rigid pavement: A random forest model hybridized with modified beetle antennae search
note: Claims to exceed MEPDG's IRI model — a comparison worth auditing in §11.

authors: Taheri, A.; Sobanjo, J.
title: Ensemble learning approach for developing performance models of flexible pavement
note: Geographically bounded training set with no out-of-region test — transferability claim untested. §11 case.

authors: Zeiada, W.; Alnaqbi, A.; Al-Khateeb, G. G.; et al.
title: Machine learning modeling of transverse cracking in flexible pavement
note: Honest reporting: R2=0.70 rather than the usual 0.95+. Useful counterexample showing what LTPP cracking data actually supports.

authors: Karballaeezadeh, N.; Mohammadzadeh S., D.; Shamshirband, S.; et al.
title: Prediction of remaining service life of pavement using an optimized support vector machine
note: Iranian case study, heavily cited; n=147 with r=0.95 — small-n pattern for §11.

authors: Sandamal, K.; Shashiprabha, S.; Muttil, N.; et al.
title: Pavement roughness prediction using explainable and supervised machine learning technique for long-term performance
note: Only two predictors (age, cumulative traffic). SHAP on a two-variable model tells you almost nothing you did not already know — a clean illustration for the §10 critique that XAI is often applied where it adds no information.

authors: Wei, X.; Wang, C.; Liu, J.; et al.
title: Optimizing faulting prediction for rigid pavements using a hybrid SHAP-TPE-CatBoost model
note: LEAKAGE CHECK REQUIRED: Boruta feature selection appears to precede the split. n=160 with 17 candidate variables and R2=0.906 — a canonical §11 case.

authors: Alnaqbi, A.; Al-Khateeb, G. G.; Zeiada, W.
title: Hybrid machine learning framework for transverse cracking prediction in CRCP with PSO and GBM
note: R2=0.99 from 33 sections under 5-fold CV. Records from the same section are not independent; unless the split is section-blocked this is textbook leakage. Priority for full-text verification.

authors: Hanandeh, S.
title: Introducing mathematical modeling to estimate pavement quality index of flexible pavements based on genetic algorithm and artificial neural networks
optimizer_hybrid: genetic algorithm (independent model, not a hybrid coupling)
note: Titled as GA+ANN but the two are run as SEPARATE competing models, not coupled — an example of the vocabulary trap in reverse (label suggests hybrid, structure does not qualify under our H1-H7 definition). Useful negative case for §2 methodology discussion.

authors: Wang, X.; Zhao, J.; Li, Q.; et al.
title: A hybrid model for prediction in asphalt pavement performance based on support vector machine and grey relation analysis
note: GRA used for feature selection before SVR — check whether selection precedes or follows the split; a leakage-risk candidate.

authors: Yu, G.; Zhang, S.; Hu, M.; et al.
title: Prediction of highway tunnel pavement performance based on digital twin and multiple time series stacking
note: Digital-twin framing gives it one of the strongest deployment-evidence codes in the corpus, though the stacking-leakage question (was CV used to select meta-features fairly?) needs full-text verification.

authors: Yao, L.; Leng, Z.; Jiang, J.; et al.
title: A multi-agent reinforcement learning model for maintenance optimization of interdependent highway pavement networks
note: Treats segment interdependence under traffic equilibrium — the network-topology argument for graph methods in §9.

authors: García-Segura, T.; Montalbán-Domingo, L.; Llopis-Castelló, D.; et al.
title: Integration of deep learning techniques and sustainability-based concepts into an urban pavement management system

authors: Barua, L.; Zou, B.
title: Planning maintenance and rehabilitation activities for airport pavements: A combined supervised machine learning and reinforcement learning approach
note: Prediction model feeds the RL environment — the coupling architecture §9 argues should be standard.

authors: Latifi, M.; Golivand Darvishvand, F.; Khandel, O.; et al.
title: A deep reinforcement learning model for predictive maintenance planning of road assets: Integrating LCA and LCCA
note: Preprint. Include only if a peer-reviewed version exists; otherwise cite as grey literature and say so.

authors: Alhussan, A. A.; Khafaga, D. S.; El-kenawy, E.-S. M.
title: Pothole and plain road classification using adaptive mutation dipper throated optimization and transfer learning for self driving cars
architecture: random forest (+ CNN feature extraction, transfer learning comparators)
optimizer_hybrid: adaptive mutation dipper-throated optimization (feature selection + hyperparameters)
note: Cited in Section 1/2 as the key evidence that a label-driven ('hybrid') search misses structurally qualifying studies: the paper never foregrounds the word hybrid, describing itself instead through the optimizer name.
